title: Cognitive macro-components and plugin architecture
tracking_rules: Update this file when a step starts, completes, changes scope, or encounters a concrete blocker.
Complete a step only when its acceptance criteria have evidence; document blocked or skipped checks.
Keep at most one step in progress and point current_step to it; use null between steps.
Treat research proposals as hypotheses until a decision or experiment supports them.
Review public-contract, schema, configuration, and deployment compatibility before implementation.
constraints: Preserve Interface -> Event/Request -> Orchestrator -> Domain -> Service.
Keep domain business policy outside orchestrator infrastructure and provider plugins.
Keep the existing public event envelope compatible.
Extend macro capabilities through versioned local plugin contracts.
Preserve existing plugin formats through adapters before adding new manifest fields.
Use explicit prediction targets and observed outcomes; keep similarity and factual reliability distinct.
Leave unrelated working-tree changes and experimental code untouched.
Require user approval for merging, tags, and production deployment.

steps.title: Remove obsolete planning and establish this tracker
acceptance_criteria: The obsolete .planning directory is removed at the user's request.
A JSON roadmap records dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, and evidence.
evidence: Removed .planning, including its tracked code map and untracked planning files.
Created steps.json from the research stages.

checks.detail: Parsed JSON and validated 12 unique ordered steps, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and progress consistency.

steps.title: Map the current macro capabilities and compatibility boundaries
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate macro capability identifies its domain, service, consumers, contracts, state, and extension points.
Representative conversation, digest, book, and hashtag flows are traced from current code.
Implemented behavior and experimental scaffolds are clearly distinguished.
Compatibility-sensitive boundaries and current gaps have source references.
Active agent instructions no longer depend on deleted planning files.
evidence: dokja_docs/capability-map.md maps policy owners, mechanisms, consumers, contracts, state, extension points, source anchors, and compatibility-sensitive gaps.
Traced conversation, digest, book, and hashtag/action/feedback flows from implementation.
Separated existing runtime wiring from the untracked Rust prediction scaffold and unverified Voice integration.
AGENTS.md now references the capability map and steps.json instead of deleted planning documents; managed blocks were preserved.
dokja_docs/README.md indexes the tracker, capability map, and research.

checks.name: documentation_validation
checks.detail: Validated 70 local links across the capability map and research, code fences, whitespace, absence of external URLs/personal paths, and documentation index entries.

checks.name: canonical_references
checks.detail: Confirmed active AGENTS.md contains no .planning references.

checks.name: runtime_tests
checks.detail: Documentation and planning inventory only; no executable implementation changed. Runtime availability remains unverified.

steps.title: Record the prototype architecture decisions
acceptance_criteria: Task scope, workspace ownership, lifecycle, limits, and persistence are explicit.
Provider, domain-policy, and workflow extension responsibilities remain distinct.
Plugin compatibility and deterministic capability-selection rules are specified.
Existing stateful service behavior and the stateless-service rule are explicitly addressed without silently changing project policy.
The first prediction target, baseline, feedback semantics, and prototype non-goals are recorded.
Research semantic relationships, runtime dependencies, feedback cycles, and orchestrator ownership before accepting ADR 0005; proposed choices must remain explicitly unresolved.
evidence: ADR 0001 specifies attempt identity, actor/channel scope, sole orchestration writer, copied boundaries, lifecycle/outcomes, initial resource limits, cancellation, volatile state, and compatibility/rollback requirements.

ADR 0002 separates provider, domain-policy, and workflow responsibilities and specifies lifecycle/API versions, legacy Feeds/Knowledge adapters, preserved legacy overrides, atomic versioned registration, deterministic bindings, and explicit fallback.

ADR 0003 preserves current repositories/caches and the canonical stateless-service rule; the volatile prototype adds no persistence, and any broader rule/storage change remains an explicit later decision.

ADR 0004 defines a 30-day explicit hashtag-feedback target, original baseline and frozen snapshots, unscored/unknown/ambiguous outcomes, controlled single-attempt attribution, scope/estimator limitations, and shadow-only evaluation.
The documentation index and capability map now link to the decision records and identify baseline capture as the next step.

ADR 0005 was withdrawn from accepted status and remains proposed. The follow-up research separates semantic, inference, runtime, and package dependencies; compares two compatible cycle owners; and distinguishes pre-action simulation from post-action observed learning using six primary/official sources.

checks.name: decision_documentation
checks.detail: Validated five decision/index documents, 97 local links across new and affected documentation, formatting, and absence of external URLs or personal paths.

checks.name: compatibility_review
checks.detail: Decisions only: no public envelope, action/route, service contract, command, SQLite schema, environment, compose, or runtime implementation changed.

checks.name: runtime_tests
checks.detail: No executable code changed. All implementation tests listed in the decisions remain requirements for later steps.

checks.name: feedback_graph_research_revision
checks.detail: Validated 95 local links, six source references, formatting, proposed ADR 0005 status, explicit decision deferral, and acyclic step dependencies. No runtime experiment was run.

steps.revision_reason: User requested research before deciding ADR 0005: Knowledge, Prediction, and Experience form a potentially cyclic graph whose execution and orchestrator boundary must be investigated.

deferred_decisions.question: Knowledge–Prediction–Experience cycle ownership, update semantics, and Book/source boundaries
deferred_decisions.implementation_gate: Resolve before step 04 integrates cognitive-loop transition contracts or any Book/Knowledge/Experience ownership migration.
deferred_decisions.allowed_before_resolution: Capture current behavior and compare pure reference loops using synthetic fixtures and fake capabilities; no production topology is adopted.

steps.completion_note: Decision/research package completed with ADR 0005 explicitly proposed and deferred to synthetic reference-loop evidence in step 03; no production topology or Book ownership change is accepted.

steps.title: Capture behavior and measurement baselines for the experiments
acceptance_criteria: Existing hashtag behavior is covered for success, abstention, missing evidence, and dependency failure.
Existing plugin compatibility and failure behavior are recorded.
Latency, invocation count, output size, and scope isolation have a reproducible measurement method.
Prediction evaluation uses later observed outcomes and a frozen baseline; data limits and skipped checks are explicit.
Compare candidate orchestrator-supervised and domain-internal reference loops with deterministic fake capabilities; do not integrate a production topology before resolving ADR 0005.
Cover cold start, missing premises, contradictory evidence, stagnation/oscillation, scope/version changes, and simulated-versus-observed outcomes.
Use comparison evidence to resolve or explicitly revise ADR 0005 before cognitive-loop contract integration or content/cognitive ownership migration.

steps.title: Implement internal typed task workspace and step outcomes
acceptance_criteria: The orchestrator owns task state and accepts typed domain results.
Evidence provenance, action proposals, execution results, and stopping reasons are represented.
Scope isolation, cancellation, bounded execution, and policy stop outcomes are tested.
The existing external envelope and response contracts remain compatible.
Resolve ADR 0005 from reference-loop evidence before integrating its transition semantics; distinguish general workspace infrastructure from still-proposed cognitive ownership.

steps.title: Introduce plugin lifecycle metadata and legacy adapters
acceptance_criteria: Identity, API version, activation, capability selection, limits, and health have explicit semantics.
Existing Feeds manifests and Knowledge registration plugins remain supported.
Unknown or incompatible versions fail with deterministic diagnostic results.
New capability bindings are configured explicitly and do not bypass domain actions.

steps.title: Run the hashtag composition experiment through the workspace
acceptance_criteria: OCR, labelled retrieval, domain selection, and execution receipts are linked to one scoped task.
A prediction snapshot precedes the action when the experiment requires that ordering.
Predictions remain in shadow mode and do not alter delivery policy.
Optional-memory failure has a defined result, and feedback links to the intended action attempt.
Success, abstention, timeout, and rejected-action paths are observable and tested.

steps.title: Run the document extractor plugin experiment
acceptance_criteria: A local extractor is added or replaced without changing router or workflow business logic.
Plugin input/output preserves the document extraction contract.
Crash, hang, malformed output, and version mismatch produce defined host behavior.
Runtime choice and operating-system permission assumptions are recorded.

steps.title: Evaluate the architecture and select the next migrations
deliverables: Decision to adopt, revise, or stop each prototype
acceptance_criteria: Existing behavior, workspace-only behavior, and shadow prediction are compared on fixed cases.
Coupling, fault containment, latency, resource use, and trace usefulness are assessed.
Prediction skill, support, and feedback coverage are reported without claiming evidence from insufficient data.
The remaining roadmap is revised from measured results before broad adoption.

steps.title: Adopt proven boundaries in conversation and delivery
acceptance_criteria: Conversation policy has one authoritative domain implementation.
System-handler responsibilities have explicit owners and focused adapters.
The adopted workspace and plugin contracts are reused only where the experiments justify them.
Existing interface commands and successful responses have regression coverage and rollback instructions.

steps.title: Define and implement required durable execution and state ownership
deliverables: Durable acceptance and recovery for selected workflows
acceptance_criteria: Each durable state kind has an owner, migration path, and rollback strategy.
Required jobs persist acceptance before acknowledgment and recover from restart.
Retries and execution receipts handle duplicates and partial failures under explicit delivery guarantees.
Any change to canonical service responsibilities is agreed before its implementation.
Affected compose files and production documentation accompany configuration or storage changes.

steps.title: Review deployment boundaries and complete the migration
acceptance_criteria: Process boundaries follow measured dependencies, resource needs, and failure-isolation requirements.
All affected module and integration checks are recorded accurately.
Architecture references, capability map, plugin documentation, and this tracker reflect delivered behavior.
Production rollout remains a separate action requiring user approval.
